speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Manpower what are the Ministry’s plans to review and enhance safety measures in the marine sector, in view of the increase in workplace fatalities in the sector in 2024.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Companies were to review their WSH management systems, reiterate senior management’s focus on safety and refresh workers’ awareness of workplace safety protocols.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Companies were also provided with materials on good safety practices and case studies to assist them in mitigating common WSH hazards in the marine sector, such as falling from height and working in confined spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This includes ensuring dive personnel are trained and use proper diving equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MPA also reminds applicants seeking a diving permit for commercial diving to adhere to the code of practice, amongst other conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: While we observe that there has been no further fatality in the marine sector in 2025 to date, we will continue to closely monitor the sector’s WSH compliance and improve its WSH performance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Together with MPA and the WSH Council, MOM will be engaging senior management of companies from the marine sector to emphasise the importance of building a strong WSH culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM will also be working with MPA to strengthen safety oversight over the marine sector, including reviewing upstream measures to further tighten diving safety standards, especially on the use of proper diving equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: I urge everyone to play our part in keeping our waters safe and befitting of Singapore’s status as a premier maritime hub.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: But for the marine sector to record five fatalities in 2024, from none in 2023, is very concerning.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I believe that the safety standards at our land-based shipyards have improved over the years and most of the recent fatality cases happened in the waters on vessels in anchorage.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I know some of these investigations are still ongoing, but can the Senior Minister of State share if MOM has a sense of what the common causes are in these cases?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Were protective gear, such as life jackets and proper diving equipment provided by the companies, worn by the workers?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Were there any links to adverse weather conditions in some of these cases?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Vessels in anchorage are considered remote sites, where it is harder for medical help to reach an injured person.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: And as we all know, response time in an emergency case can be a matter of life and death.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Could response time therefore be a contributory factor in these cases because they happen on remote sites?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: If so, are there any plans to improve the response time of emergency medical help to these remote sites?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If we look at the situation last year, indeed, as the Member pointed out, the anchorages were the point of concern, while shipyards have improved.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But over time, if we look at the last five years, for example, I would say it is about 50-50.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But that does not mean that we take our eyes off our shipyards as well because if you look at the issues at the shipyards, it is not necessarily at the shipyard itself, but it could also be the ancillary activities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The one incident that we had at the shipyard was a worker being struck by a forklift.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, it is not so much shipbuilding, but ancillary activities around the shipyard.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: There was another case of a worker being struck by the propeller of a boat during diving works – that was an unfortunate accident.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: There were others where workers fell from the vessel.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If I recall correctly, a safety vest was used but still, unfortunately, perhaps due to the waters.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The numbers are quite small, therefore, you have different incidents and there is no clear pattern.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But certainly, we will look to see how we can improve.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think those are also important aspects, where we can help to mitigate some of the risks while waiting for the medical personnel to come.
